cleaned_body_text: Aotearoa New Zealand oceans are large, diverse and extremely valuable. They support most of the country’s wildlife, a sizeable blue economy, and have strong cultural and social values. Although often perceived as wild and untouched, the oceans are experiencing profound and increasing impacts from human activity. It is the inshore coastal ecosystems that are degrading the most, due to multiple anthropogenic pressures from land and sea activities. Over the years, there have been numerous reports and scientific papers that essentially reach the same conclusions. Our oceans governance system is not up to the job of managing the oceans well and we need to urgently fix it. In this report we have provided recommendations for how to do this. They include developing a National Oceans Strategy, National Marine Spatial Planning Framework, Marine Protected Areas Act and Oceans Act along with establishing an Oceans Commission to act as a champion for the ocean. The time has now long passed for talking – we need to get on with oceans reform.
